Introduction of the County and About This Article

Audrain County is in central Missouri. The county seat is Mexico, Missouri. People and investors often want to know how property tax sales work here. This guide explains the tax sale process step by step. It answers key questions about timing, location, rules, bidding steps, redemption rights and more. You will learn what to expect at an Audrain County tax deed sale and how to prepare.

What Is the County’s Tax Deed Process

Audrain County holds a delinquent property tax sale under Missouri law. If taxes on a property are unpaid for several years, the county offers the property at public auction. The auction sells the right to purchase the lien or deed for that property. The process is public and bidders can compete. Successful bidders may earn return on investment or may gain title if the property is not redeemed.

Important Details

Key Takeaways
  • Audrain County hosts a delinquent property tax sale annually on the fourth Monday in August, starting at 10 AM Central Time.
  • Bidders must register in advance, and the auction takes place in the Community Room of the Audrain County Courthouse.
  • Successful bidders receive a certificate of purchase and have one year to allow the original owner to redeem the property.
  • Investors should conduct due diligence to check for liens, property conditions, and tax records before participating in the sale.
  • Audrain County’s stable economy and moderate property prices make it an attractive option for tax deed investing.

What You Need to Know

When Are Tax Sales Held?

Every year the county holds its tax sale on the fourth Monday in August. The auction begins at 10 AM Central Time. This schedule follows Missouri statute and county policy.

You can check the collector’s office announcements or calendar for upcoming dates. The county usually updates details before the sale by publishing notices on its website.

Is Registration Required?

Yes. Bidders must register before they can participate. The county places a list of properties eligible for sale online and in public notices before the auction. You must register with the county office before the sale. Details on registration deadlines are published ahead of the sale.

Where Is the Auction Held?

Tax sales in Audrain County are held in the Community Room of the Audrain County Courthouse. The address is:

Audrain County Courthouse
101 North Jefferson Street
Mexico, Missouri 65265

This is the official site where live bidding happens.

Redemption Period in Missouri

Under Missouri law, after a tax sale, the property owner generally has about one year to redeem the property. This means the owner can pay the full amount owed (including taxes, penalty, interest) within that time and reclaim the property even after sale.

If a property does not sell at the first or second sale, and later sells, the redemption period may be shorter in certain cases. You should check local rules for specifics.

Bidding Procedure and Terms

At the tax sale:

The county offers parcels for sale in public auction.
Bidding starts at the amount of taxes owed plus interest and fees.
Bidders compete until the highest offer is reached.
The highest bidder wins the certificate of purchase.

You pay the total bid amount on the day of the sale. A recording fee and other minor charges are also collected.

You do not receive title at the sale. You get a certificate of purchase. The original owner still has rights to redeem until redemption expires.

Who Should I Contact for Help?

For more information, you can contact the Audrain County Collector of Revenue. Their official contact email often used for tax sale inquiries is available on county tax sale resources:
kbecker@audraincounty.org (Audrain County Treasurer/Collector office).

You can also contact the county office by phone to confirm details.

The best sources for updates are:

  • The Audrain County Official Website – Official announcements and tax sale lists are posted here.
  • Audrain County Back Tax Sale FAQ page – Updated answers on procedures.
  • Local newspapers – Counties list properties and sale details publicly before the auction.

Fun Facts About Audrain County

  • Audrain County was established in the early 1800s.
  • The county seat is Mexico, known for annual cultural events.
  • Agriculture is a strong part of the local economy.
  • Audrain County has rich history in railroad and grain trade.

Attractions & Economic Highlights

  • Long Branch State Park and natural areas.
  • Mexico Towne Centre and historic downtown.
  • Major roads connect to I 70 and US highways.
  • Agriculture, local manufacturing, and services drive jobs.

Why This County Appeals to Investors

  • Property markets with older homes and rural land give entry points.
  • One year redemption offers time before title rights.
  • Tax sale yields in Missouri can provide high returns with low-risk investment when done right.
  • State tax sale law supports investor participation in sales.

Auction Process for Tax Sales

How the Auction Works

  1. Bidders attend live at the courthouse.

  2. Properties are offered one by one.

  3. The minimum bid starts at taxes owed.

  4. Bidding continues until no higher bids.

  5. Winning bidder pays and receives certificate.

Maximum and Expected Returns

In Missouri, tax deed purchases can return interest or title value if the owner does not redeem. Exact returns vary based on bid price, property value and redemption action. Investors often use the one year redemption to plan exit or resale. The interest paid on redemption can add to yields.

Foreign Investor Participation

Missouri does not restrict non residents from bid. Investors from anywhere can bid as long as they register and meet county requirements. This opens up global investment opportunities for tax sale bidders.

Importance of Due Diligence

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check tax records for unpaid taxes.
  • Inspect property condition.
  • Check for liens or other claims.
  • Estimate repair costs and market value.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • Hidden liens and costs can reduce value.
  • Property may have title issues.
  • You may overpay without knowing risks.

Why Audrain County Is a Top Choice

Economy and Local Conditions

  • Stable rural economy helps long term property values.
  • Easy access to major roads adds appeal.

Real Estate Overview

Property prices in Audrain County are generally moderate. This can make tax sale investing a way to access real estate at lower entry costs. Investors should review local sales and property values before bidding.

Conclusion

Audrain County’s tax sale process is structured under Missouri law. It offers opportunities for investors who want to buy tax deed properties at auction. The county provides clear schedules, rules and notices. Investing here requires planning and research. Learning the auction steps, redemption rules, and doing property checks helps you make better decisions. Always use official county announcements as your source before bidding.

Pro Tips

  • Visit the courthouse before the sale to see how auctions run.
  • Use the county property search tools to study parcels.
  • Have funds ready before the auction.
  • Track local property values in Mexico and other towns.
  • Check for liens and title issues early.

Common Questions After the Auction

Can I inspect property before redemption ends?

Yes.

Do I get title right away?

Not until redemption and process complete.

What fees are added?

Recording and processing fees

What if no one bids?

The county may take ownership

Can I sell my certificate?

Yes, depending on rules.
